context: The branch carries a prototype approved on screen by the maintainer: the two templates and agreement.js are kept exactly as they are and are not under review. The Python behind them was removed (T001) and is rebuilt test-first by the plan. The spec was amended at the prototype review (decisions.md D14): the page lists and links to each document and does not show wording. Which documents are 'required' belongs to a later feature (issue #87); here every outstanding document is required and the view exposes is_optional() returning False (D16). Standing rules for this repo: no leading-underscore names, line length 88, no compatibility aliases, no test of text content or of layout, alignment or badge variant, Cotton components and never {% include %} partials.
orchestrator_question: Verify against the RESOLVED packages and this repo, both sides of each rule: (1) research.md says bulk_create(ignore_conflicts=True) through AcceptanceQuerySet.bulk_create writes new acceptances and passes over existing ones in one statement, with the notice refusal in one query: read models.py AcceptanceQuerySet.bulk_create and Acceptance.save and say what bulk_create skips that record() does (is_published check, subject_of, immutability) and whether plan.md's record_many covers each. (3) FR-008 and FR-012 with a required document left unagreed: plan step 4/5 records the partial agreement and re-renders; is any scenario in spec.md undemonstrated by tasks.md? Give counts: FR against tasks N of 26, SC against tasks N of 9. (4) get_destination(): name every input url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme lets through that would still leave the site or loop back to the page. (5) Is any planned test a change detector, or a test of wording or appearance?
